The text below is drawn from , a measure of the priorities of the British electorate.



Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
This manifesto sets out proposals across immigration, public spending, taxation, public services, energy, policing, justice, education, welfare, Brexit, defence, housing, families, infrastructure, agriculture, fisheries, pensions/social care, constitutional change, and governance, with associated costings and savings.

Core pledges:
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; detain and remove illegal arrivals; new immigration department; offshore processing; restrict student dependants; 5‑year residency for benefits; higher employer NI (20%) for foreign workers with exemptions.
- Zero NHS waiting lists by using independent capacity, tax incentives for staff, vouchers when waiting times exceed set limits, and efficiency reforms.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; scrap energy levies and VAT on energy; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Reduce government waste via departmental efficiency (5%), ending interest on QE reserves, halving foreign aid, improving tax collection, and deregulation.

Tax and economy:
- Personal: Lift income tax start point to £20k; higher rate from £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap energy levies and VAT on bills; cut stamp duty (0% under £750k, 2% to £1.5m, 4% above); restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; reform inheritance tax (no IHT under £2m; 20% above with charity option).
- Business: Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k profits; cut main rate to 20% then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; simplify planning; reduce employment regulation; simplify the tax code.

NHS and social care:
- Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS and social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; write off student fees pro‑rata over 10 years of NHS service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; weekend theatres; better procurement; “Pharmacy First” approach; public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Royal Commission on social care; close tax loopholes for offshore care‑home structures.

Energy and environment:
- Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale; develop SMRs and other technologies.

Law, order, and justice:
- Recruit 40,000 police; increase stop and search; tougher sentences (including mandatory life for violent repeat offenders); expand prison capacity by 10,000 places; increase criminal justice budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; revise hate‑crime definitions; streamline policing, reduce paperwork.

Education:
- Curriculum review; restrict gender identity policies in schools; ensure single‑sex facilities and parental notification; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans and extend repayment; enforce entry standards; expand pupil referral units; promote 2‑year degrees.

Welfare and work:
- Incentivise work via higher tax threshold; target up to 2 million back to work; two‑strike rule on job offers; face‑to‑face assessments with exemptions for severe conditions.

Brexit and sovereignty:
- Scrap retained EU laws; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

Defence and veterans:
- Raise defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% by year 6; pay review; legal protections; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30,000 for the army; reform procurement.

Housing:
- Fast‑track brownfield development; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; strengthen leaseholder protections.

Infrastructure and transport:
- Cancel remaining HS2; repeal ULEZ/low‑traffic schemes; no bans on petrol/diesel; accelerate regional road/rail upgrades; new utility ownership model (50% public/50% UK pension funds); cap standing charges.

Agriculture and fisheries:
- Increase farm budget to £3bn; replace climate‑linked subsidies; tackle supermarket power; “Buy British” targets; cut red tape; restrict foreign fishing access; expand patrols; rebuild processing.

Constitution and governance:
- Leave the ECHR; reform the House of Lords and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; consider PR via referendum; British Bill of Rights; overhaul equalities and free‑speech laws; reform the BBC funding model; new anti‑corruption unit; oppose WHO pandemic treaty and a CBDC; retain cash.

Funding summary (annualised):
- Claimed savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from growth assumptions.
- Claimed costs: ~£141bn.

TEXT_C:
Summary of proposals (non-ideological)

Health and care
- NHS: Extra revenue funding rising from £8bn in year one to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Targets include faster GP access, same‑day urgent GP access, guaranteed NHS dentistry, a National Cancer Plan, and 28‑day access to evidence‑based mental health therapies. £1.5bn public health uplift; primary care: +£1.5bn/year by 2030 and £2bn capital. Dentistry: +£3bn/year by 2030 and a new NHS contract. School counsellor in every school. Support for assisted dying (with safeguards). Aim to end new HIV transmissions by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/year investment; national career structure and better pay; reforms to protect overseas care workers; “Care Supporter” right. Disability: immediate 5% benefit uplift; oppose replacing PIP cash with vouchers; SEND travel support. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils.

Homes and planning
- 150,000 new social homes/year; end no‑fault evictions; empower local rent controls; end “right to buy.” New homes to Passivhaus‑equivalent with solar and low‑carbon heat; upgrade PRS to EPC C. Retrofit programme: £29bn home insulation, £4bn public buildings insulation, £9bn low‑carbon heating, £7bn heat-resilience (five‑year totals). Bring empty homes into use; stronger local planning, lower embodied carbon, reuse demolition materials; reduce car dependence.

Energy and climate
- No new oil and gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax starting ~£120/tCO2, rising to up to £500/t within 10 years. Wind to ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; lift onshore wind constraints; minimum community ownership share; expand grid, storage, interconnectors; green hydrogen for industry. Stop new nuclear and phase out existing stations.

Economy, taxation, and public ownership
- Green transition investment averaging £40bn/year (power, retrofits, rail, active travel, industry, water/sewage). Bring rail, water, and major retail energy suppliers into public ownership. Wealth tax: 1% on assets >£10m, 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and pension relief. Higher windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; VAT cuts for hospitality/arts and rises for private education/financial services. Council tax revaluation and steps toward land value taxation. Regional mutual banks (+£10bn capital). R&D +£30bn over five years. Estimated additional annual receipts by end of parliament: personal/wealth £50–70bn; carbon tax up to ~£80bn; business taxes +£40bn over five years. Borrowing to invest within inflation constraints.

Work and incomes
- Charter of Workers’ Rights; repeal recent restrictions on industrial action; minimum wage £15/hour (all ages) with support for SMEs; 10:1 pay ratio cap; day‑one rights; gig workers classed as “workers”; safe sick pay; progress toward a four‑day week. Welfare: +£40/week to UC/legacy benefits; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; 5% disability uplift; carers’ allowance +10%; protect pension uprating; end sanctions; long‑term move to Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% of land and sea by 2030; public ownership of water; DEFRA +£1.5bn; Right to Roam Act; peat re‑wetting; fully protected MPAs; ban destructive fishing in MPAs. Animal Protection Commission; ban blood sports; end factory‑farming cages/routine antibiotics; end badger cull. Nearly triple farm support; cut pesticides; boost horticulture; free school meals for all children and breakfast clubs; local food partnerships and waste reduction.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/year to fix unsafe buildings; SEND +£5bn; counsellors and school nurses restored; reduce high‑stakes testing; Natural History GCSE; bring academies under local control; charge VAT on private school fees. Early years: Sure Start +£1.4bn/year; extend funded childcare to 35 hours/week from 9 months. Post‑16/FE: sixth‑form +£3bn; FE skills +£12bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees and restore grants.

Transport
- Raise public transport subsidies to £10bn/year; +£19bn over five years for public transport, electrification, and active travel; public ownership of rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycling/walking. Oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; develop road pricing; ICE sales end by 2027, road use by 2035; EV scrappage rising to £5bn/year; more HGV rail freight. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion; tax kerosene; ban domestic flights where rail <3 hours.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture, digital, justice, foreign policy
- Proportional representation; votes at 16; elected second chamber; scrap voter ID; tighter lobbying/think‑tank transparency; expand devolution; defend Human Rights Act; repeal recent protest‑curbing laws; self‑ID for trans people.
- Migration/asylum: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work while claims processed; remove spousal income rules; simplify visas; free NHS for visa holders; voting rights for visa‑holding residents; create a Department of Migration.
- Arts/media/digital: £5bn over five years for local arts/sport; VAT exemption for cultural events; media ownership cap (≤20% per market); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation and creator IP protection.
- Justice/policing: restore trust, end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; domestic abuse priority; decriminalise sex work; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; expand diversion and restorative justice; invest ~£11bn over parliament in courts/legal aid/judges.
- International: support Ukraine; aim to rejoin EU (steps: customs union, free movement, Erasmus); sign the UN nuclear ban treaty, cancel Trident; NATO reform (no first use). Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss & Damage; debt relief; support ecocide law. Israel–Palestine: immediate bilateral ceasefire, recognition of Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel, war‑crimes investigations.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_C better reflects what these voters cared about.
